Tollgate Community Junior School
At Tollgate, we live by the motto of 'Together Everyone Achieves More'. We are a 'Tollgate Family' and work together for the shared success of our whole community.
We are very proud of our children; their behaviour, enthusiasm for learning and kindness towards others enable them to gain a well-developed understanding of the world and their role within it.
The committed staff team at Tollgate work hard to ensure our curriculum is exciting and relevant to our children. We make great use of our fantastic school grounds, utilise the local area and ensure the children's learning is enriched through trips and workshops, bringing the curriculum to life.
Through a strong pastoral offer, we are able to support our children as and when the moment arises. Inclusion is central to our vision of excellence for all, and we ensure children with Special Educational Needs are provided with the support needed to thrive in and beyond our school.
Should you want to see our fantastic school in action, please do not hesitate to contact the school office to arrange a tour.

AMAZING Keep it up Tollgate Family
Last Thursday the Mini Police were invited to the Police station. The children met a member of the Traffic Police Team and talked about all things road safety. The children also got to take part in a forensics activity and took samples of their own finger prints. A very fun and informative afternoon was had by all.
To all Year 6 Parents, As a team, we just wanted to say a big thank you to all the parents for everything they did last week - whether it was packing bags for the residential, washing PE kits after the Colour Run or making sure water bottles were filled for all of those hot days. Your support is very much appreciated and makes the last few days that we have with the children that bit easier and more enjoyable for them. Going into the last full week we just wanted to send out a reminder of a few things as you know, there is a lot going on: The production will be in full swing this week with shows happening during school time and in the evenings. If your child can attend in the evenings to perform or work backstage, we really appreciate it. There are still opportunities to get tickets (2 per child) to come and enjoy the show. They've worked so hard and it looks and sounds fantastic so far! Show times are as follows: Wednesday 15th July: Performance of 'Joseph' – 6.00pm Thursday 16th July: Performance of 'Joseph' – 2:00pm Friday 17th July: Performance of 'Joseph'– 6.30pm The children will be completing their autograph/memory books from this week. We would like to include pictures of their classmates in them, so we are having an 'opt-out' system for photographs. If you really don't want your child's image to be in the autograph book of another child, then please let their teacher know. If we don't hear from you, then we will assume it is fine to include your child in any group pictures with their friends that they want to take. Monday 20th July: Year 6 Prom! 6 - 8 pm Tuesday 21st July: The children's leaver's assembly is at 9:15 and parents are welcome to attend. Children can bring an additional shirt in for signing (not the one they are wearing). Felt tip pens for this is fine, no Sharpies as they go through onto the tables and other side of the shirts. Collection/leaving time on the last day is 1:30pm. Thank you in advance for all the help in giving the children a nice send off at the end of their time at Tollgate. The Year 6 Team.
School perfomances: We would like to clarify timings for any children involved in this week's very exciting Joseph performances, particularly in light of England progressing to the semi-finals of the World Cup and the match time for Wednesday. Wednesday Due to the original timings leading to the production clashing with the England vs Argentina match, we have adjusted our timings slightly to enable families to enjoy both events. We appreciate the difficulty in the change of times, but we recognise many families would not want to miss the football and we would hate people to have to leave the production early. Children involved in the production need to be dropped back in school at 5.15pm. The performance will now begin for families at 6pm, with doors open fifteen minutes before. They will then be dismissed from the playground as soon as possible (maintaining safety procedures) after the production finishes, enabling families to get back home for the match. Thursday The performance is at 2.00pm. The children will not quite be finished for the normal end of day time, so we ask that families come to collect at 3.45pm from the playground. We will do our best to get the children out as quickly as possible to you. Friday The timings will remain as originally published. The children need to be dropped back in school at 5.45pm. The performance will start at 6.30pm, with doors open fifteen minutes before. They will then be dismissed from the playground as soon as possible after the production finishes. Thank you for your support of this event and your child(ren)'s ambitions and talents - it promises to be a wonderful performance.
Dear Year 6 Parents and Carers, Thank you so much for your incredibly generous monetary donations. Thanks to your kindness and support, we have now raised enough money to organise everything the children requested for their Year 6 Leavers' Prom. We are so grateful for your generosity. However, at this stage, we would be especially grateful for donations of the physical items listed below so that the students can get busy creating decorations for their special evening. If you are able to donate any of the following decoration items, please send them into school next week: White fairy lights Cardboard for making decorative stars Black, white and gold tissue paper If you are able to donate any of the following food and drink items, please bring them into school on the morning of the prom, Monday 20th July: Chocolates Strawberries Marshmallows Crisps Cookies Thank you once again for helping us make this such a memorable celebration for our Year 6 leavers. Your continued support is hugely appreciated. Kind regards, The Tollgate Leavers' Prom Team

Reading at Home
Accelerated Reader
At Tollgate, we love reading. We want all our children to become fluent, accurate readers. Our aim is to encourage a lifelong love of reading. Accelerated Reader (AR) is a computer-based reading program to help with this.
We know that children who read books that are too easy or too hard for them become bored and may give up reading.
With AR we help your child pick a book at their level, which they read at their own pace. This way they are more likely to enjoy reading and progress in their learning.
When they finish the book, they take a short quiz on the computer at school. Children record their quiz scores in their reading diary.
Children do not have to take a quiz for every book they read, but they tend to enjoy taking them. The quizzes show whether your child understood what they read. With this feedback the teacher can help your child set targets and ongoing reading practice.
Your child’s teacher will also share reports with you on how they are doing through the year.
Children take a Star Reading test to find out their reading level. They do this four times a year:
This helps identify a range of books that will challenge but not frustrate your child. Books on the scheme have a book level (difficulty) and an interest level (themes and ideas).
As with anything, ability improves with practice. Encourage your child to read at home. Show that you value reading. Reading with your child, no matter what their age, helps build a love of reading and learning.
According to research, children who read at least 35 minutes a day with good understanding see the greatest gains. At Tollgate, we have a ‘Read and Relax’ session in school each day for 20 minutes. We expect each child to read at home for 15 minutes each day
You can help your child find books that are interesting to them. Visit the website and click on ‘Advanced Search’.
You can search for titles based on their Book and Interest Levels. Choose from fiction or non-fiction on a range of topics. Get a copy at home, in class or from the school library.
